notes:
Account background: fintech risk engine + customer communications stack. Heavy real-time personalization at edge; mandates strict residency for EU customers and on-prem options for regulated flows. Eng team is skeptical of warm-pool promises due to past cold-start incidents with other vendors.

Primary ask: dedicated GPU reservation with firm throughput guarantees and documented latency SLOs. Wants a plan for autoscaling that avoids request queue pile-up during European market opens (08:00-10:00 CET) and US morning ramp.

Detailed POC acceptance criteria (from SE alignment call):
- Sustained throughput: 250 qps for 6 hours with p50 < 40ms, p95 < 150ms end-to-end for short-completion chat prompts (<= 128 tokens).
- Burst handling: absorb 1k qps spikes for up to 5 minutes with graceful degradation rules.
- Cold-start time for model variant start: <= 8s (target) with warm-pool of standby GPUs.
- Queueing: request queue depth must stay below 200 requests; auto-reject or backpressure policy documented when exceeded.
- Cost predictability: reserved GPU plan + scale-to-zero disallowed for regulated flows; need monthly capacity forecast and overage billing cap.
- Audit/compliance: KMS key control, retention controls, SSO/SAML integration proof.

Autoscaling/Capacity management preferences captured on last call:
- Preferred scale-up triggers: combined metric of GPU utilization > 72% OR queue depth > 60 requests OR sustained RPS growth > 25% in rolling 2-minute window.
- Preferred scale-down triggers: utilization < 35% AND queue depth < 10 for 15 minutes cooldown. Avoid aggressive scale-down during EU trading hours.
- Warm pool: propose warm pool of 8–12 GPUs per region (EU/NA) with prioritized warmup for primary model variants. Warm pool should be billed as reserved-but-idle capacity in contract.
- Pre-warming strategy: scheduled pre-warm based on forecasted calendar events (market opens, major releases). Support predictive pre-warm via historical traffic ingestion (CSV or API).
- Fast-path fallback: configured fallback to smaller quantized model variant (8-bit) with explicit quality-loss threshold and automatic rollback if quality drops below acceptance.
- Queueing behavior: FIFO with priority tagging (premium customers), explicit backpressure HTTP 429 pattern for non-critical requests. Circuit-breaker to fail fast for sustained >10% error rate over 1 minute.

SLA negotiation notes:
- Customer insists on written SLA with credits tied to p99 latency breaches and throughput shortfalls. Wants per-route SLOs for payment/checkout vs personalization.
- Request to cap overage charges during first 6 months of POC. Legal wants to review Redwood's force-majeure and maintenance windows.
